# Paid Live Mission 6 — the tool that lies about paths on Windows.
#
# ONE FILE, AND ITS TYPE IMPORTS VANISH. `node-tool-adapter.ts` imports only Node
# builtins plus a TYPE-ONLY import from the Julius barrel, and this repository
# runs TypeScript through Node's own type stripping — so the type import is erased
# before anything executes and pulls nothing into the sandbox. The closure is
# therefore this single file, which is what makes this mission small enough to be
# a representative one rather than an endurance test.
#
# THE BUDGET NEEDS NO FOUNDER DECISION, which is part of why this mission was
# chosen. Every raised ceiling in `scripts/julius-live-contract-check.mjs` is a
# recorded founder decision; this contract stays inside the DEFAULT bound of $5
# and one repair cycle, so nothing about it needs authorising beyond the paid
# dispatch itself. The bound is defensible from the two paid datapoints: Mission 4
# settled $1.390954 for a ~200-line module and Mission 5 $5.177120 for three
# integrated files, against this mission's one 63-line file and a narrow change.
# One repair cycle is enough to prove the repair path WORKS if the reviewer finds
# a genuine defect; it is not an instruction to find one.
#
# The seeded specification (`seed/.../node-tool-search-paths.test.ts`) is
# provisioned beside it and is NOT listed here: it is the mission's specification,
# not its deliverable, and the contract forbids editing it.
src/relay/workspace/julius-tools/node-tool-adapter.ts
